name: css-card-stacking
title: CSS Card Stacking
description: A full-screen section where tilted coloured cards stay pinned to the viewport and pile up on top of each other while the page scrolls, with a fixed heading beside them.
use: Several feature cards should be read one after another without losing the reader's place on the page.
avoid: Each card needs a full screen height, so a short page or a busy dashboard wastes vertical space.
a11y: Smooth scrolling ignores prefers-reduced-motion, and the view buttons have no visible focus style. (keyboard: yes, labels: partial, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: A dark navy page with a faint grid. Large rounded cards in green, pink, orange and blue sit tilted a few degrees, each holding a bold title, a short paragraph and a small black button. A fixed heading sits to the right of the stack.
behaves: On scroll each card holds its place while the next rises and covers it, so earlier cards remain as a thin top edge. The side heading stays put throughout; scrolling back peels the cards away in reverse.
customise: Card titles, copy, colours and links are written into the markup for each card; add or remove stacking blocks to change the pile. Scroll easing comes from the smooth-scroll wrapper.
weight: light: Pure CSS sticky cards plus a smooth-scroll wrapper; little work happens per frame.
